services.availabilityNote: Available by agreement. Scope, access, product readiness, timing and terms are confirmed before kickoff; a pilot is not a general-availability SaaS subscription.
services.label: Poesis Pilot
services.title: Prove the value in your own context.
services.summary: Evaluate Poesis against a real organizational problem, with an agreed scope, a baseline and evidence that supports your next investment decision.
services.lead: Before committing to a transformation, establish what Poesis can change in the work that matters to you. Start with the value you seek, the pain you face and a result you can judge.
services.proposition: A guided ITIP + SIE evaluation connects your chosen needs to a feasible product scope. Together we agree the evidence, responsibilities and decision criteria, then distinguish demonstrated value from work that remains ahead.

outcomes.title: A decision-ready brief
outcomes.description: A shared problem statement, selected use cases, data boundaries and explicit success criteria.

outcomes.title: Evidence in your context
outcomes.description: An evaluation of the agreed scope against the baseline, including limitations and unmet needs.

outcomes.title: A justified next step
outcomes.description: A recommendation to proceed, refine or stop, with dependencies and further investment made explicit.

stages.title: Frame
stages.description: Choose a worthwhile problem and agree feasibility, access, terms and evidence before kickoff.

stages.title: Evaluate
stages.description: Exercise the agreed workflows with your examples and review results with the people accountable for the work.

stages.title: Decide
stages.description: Compare the evidence with success criteria and identify the smallest justified next commitment.

services.availabilityNote: Planned advisory and transformation offer. Autonomy is a progressive design objective, not a claim of a fully autonomous enterprise or an available end-to-end delivery service.
services.label: Autonomous Enterprise Transformation
services.title: Design the organization that can govern its own evolution.
services.summary: Connect strategy, decision rights, organizational design and feedback into a practical path toward greater autonomy, without losing human accountability.
services.lead: Automating disconnected tasks does not make an enterprise autonomous. Leaders need an operating model in which people, AI and software act toward shared purposes, within explicit authority, and adapt from evidence.
services.proposition: Poesis approaches transformation through systemics: define purposes and functions, expose dependencies, establish governance and close feedback loops. GSM supplies a common language for the organization's definitions; SIE is designed to govern their evolution and execution. The engagement translates that architecture into a staged transformation, beginning where value and controllability can be demonstrated.

outcomes.title: An explicit target operating model
outcomes.description: Purpose, functions, responsibilities and decision rights connected across organizational boundaries, with human authority preserved.

outcomes.title: A sequenced transformation portfolio
outcomes.description: Prioritized changes selected for systemic impact, feasibility and risk, with dependencies and acceptance criteria.

outcomes.title: A measurable autonomy roadmap
outcomes.description: Defined delegation boundaries, escalation paths and feedback measures that determine when greater autonomy is justified.

stages.title: Diagnose the system
stages.description: Map strategic intent, operating tensions, decision delays and the gaps between governance and actual work.

stages.title: Design the transition
stages.description: Define the target model, governance changes and first transformation increment with accountable owners.

stages.title: Learn before expanding
stages.description: Plan bounded evaluations and review their evidence before extending delegation or organizational scope.

services.availabilityNote: Planned service, including use case discovery. Delivery scope, integrations and operating capacity are not yet offered as a standard engagement; a Poesis Pilot can be discussed separately.
services.label: Agentic Transformation
services.title: Find the work worth delegating. Make delegation accountable.
services.summary: Discover and prioritize agentic use cases, redesign the workflows around them, and define how results, cost and risk will be evaluated.
services.lead: An impressive agent demonstration is not an operating capability. The opportunity lies in choosing work where AI can produce useful results, giving it the right context and tools, and knowing when a person must decide.
services.proposition: Poesis connects use case discovery to workflow and governance design. The planned approach draws on SAF's explicit roles, instructions, artifact contracts and human gates, with GSM-based organizational definitions to anchor context. Each candidate is assessed against simpler automation, integration effort and measurable value before agentic complexity is introduced.

outcomes.title: A ranked use case portfolio
outcomes.description: Opportunities assessed for business value, frequency, context readiness, integration cost and consequences of failure.

outcomes.title: Workflows with clear authority
outcomes.description: Human and agent roles, tool permissions, handoffs, review gates and escalation paths designed around the work.

outcomes.title: An evaluation and adoption plan
outcomes.description: Representative cases, quality thresholds, latency and cost budgets, plus ownership and training for day-to-day use.

stages.title: Discover
stages.description: Investigate real tasks with their owners and shortlist opportunities where delegation can improve an observable result.

stages.title: Engineer the workflow
stages.description: Specify context, tools, instructions and controls; define a bounded implementation and the tests it must pass.

stages.title: Evaluate and adopt
stages.description: Use evidence from representative work to decide what to automate, retain under review or leave with people.

services.availabilityNote: Planned service. Source access, modeling scope and consuming tools will be agreed per engagement; automated sourcing and runtime integrations remain subject to product readiness.
services.label: Organizational Context Engineering
services.title: Give humans and AI a shared understanding of the organization.
services.summary: Turn fragmented organizational knowledge into structured, governed context: purposes, responsibilities, dependencies, rules and the evidence behind them.
services.lead: Documents can tell an agent what was written. They do not necessarily tell it which definition is current, who has authority, what depends on a decision or which constraints apply. Useful organizational context must make those distinctions explicit.
services.proposition: Poesis uses GSM to structure organizational definitions and SIE's lifecycle design to distinguish proposed knowledge from accepted authority. The planned engagement combines domain modeling, source mapping, provenance and review with task-specific context contracts. It complements retrieval and prompt engineering by defining what retrieved information means and when it is fit to guide action.

outcomes.title: A coherent organizational model
outcomes.description: A scoped vocabulary connecting purposes, functions, responsibilities, interactions and governing constraints.

outcomes.title: Traceable, reviewable context
outcomes.description: Source provenance, ownership and revision rules that separate observations and proposals from accepted definitions.

outcomes.title: Context contracts for consumers
outcomes.description: Defined information needs, access boundaries, freshness criteria and evaluation cases for humans, agents and applications.

stages.title: Map the decisions
stages.description: Identify who needs context, what decisions it must support and where incomplete or contradictory information causes failure.

stages.title: Model and reconcile
stages.description: Structure the relevant knowledge, expose conflicts and agree who can review and accept each definition.

stages.title: Connect and evaluate
stages.description: Design supported retrieval and integration paths, then test relevance, traceability and freshness on representative tasks.

services.availabilityNote: Planned managed application; no self-service subscription is available. Hosting, tenancy, integrations, supported features and service commitments require acceptance before launch.
services.label: ITIP SaaS
services.title: Turn IT knowledge into better-governed decisions.
services.summary: A planned managed IT Intelligence Platform for application and service context, dependency analysis, governance review and evidence-led IT decisions.
services.lead: IT leaders and architects need to understand what they operate, how it supports the business and where change creates exposure. That understanding is hard to maintain when inventories, architecture models and compliance evidence evolve separately.
services.proposition: ITIP is the IT-domain application over SIE: a shared workspace designed to connect IT definitions, relationships, governance and appraisal in the language of IT work. The SaaS offer is intended to provide that application without requiring customers to assemble and operate the underlying platform. It differs from SIE SaaS by delivering the IT-facing experience, not just engine APIs.

outcomes.title: Shared IT context
outcomes.description: A planned governed view of applications, services, responsibilities and dependencies, with source coverage and unresolved gaps visible.

outcomes.title: Evidence-led change decisions
outcomes.description: Designed support for dependency and impact analysis, architecture reviews and prioritization against business concerns.

outcomes.title: Governance in daily IT work
outcomes.description: A planned review and appraisal experience connecting applicable constraints, findings and accountable follow-up.

stages.title: Choose the first IT scope
stages.description: Identify an application or service portfolio, decision owners and the decisions the workspace should improve.

stages.title: Establish trusted context
stages.description: Agree source coverage, reconcile definitions and configure the supported governance and review scope.

stages.title: Embed in decision routines
stages.description: Introduce the workspace into architecture, change and appraisal reviews, measuring usefulness and information freshness.

services.availabilityNote: Planned managed engine; no production API subscription is available. API scope, isolation, security, recovery, quotas and service commitments must be validated before launch.
services.label: SIE SaaS
services.title: Build on governed definitions, not another isolated knowledge store.
services.summary: A planned managed Systemic Intelligence Engine for builders integrating GSM definitions, lifecycle governance and controlled execution into their own applications.
services.lead: Application and AI platform builders need more than storage: they need a consistent way to type organizational knowledge, control its evolution and distinguish accepted definitions from tentative contributions.
services.proposition: SIE provides the engine layer behind Poesis. Its architecture combines definition management, lifecycle governance, collaborative sourcing and governed mechanism execution. The SaaS offer is intended to expose an agreed set of these services through managed interfaces, so customers can build domain applications and integrations without operating the full engine stack. Unlike ITIP SaaS, it does not supply an IT-domain user workspace.

outcomes.title: A governed definition foundation
outcomes.description: Planned managed access to typed, versioned definitions and lifecycle controls for your application domain.

outcomes.title: Controlled integration contracts
outcomes.description: Explicit APIs, identities, authorization boundaries and provenance requirements for applications and agent tooling.

outcomes.title: An agreed operational boundary
outcomes.description: A defined split between managed engine responsibilities and your domain logic, models, tools and downstream effects.

stages.title: Define the application contract
stages.description: Identify the domain model, consuming applications and engine services required, including non-functional needs.

stages.title: Qualify the integration
stages.description: Test the supported interfaces, lifecycle behavior and tenant boundaries against representative workloads.

stages.title: Prepare for operation
stages.description: Agree monitoring, change handling, recovery and exit arrangements before considering a production commitment.

services.availabilityNote: Planned Poesis-issued practitioner qualification in GSM. No credential is currently awarded; this is neither external standards-body accreditation nor certification of an organization's compliance.
services.label: GSM Certification
services.title: Demonstrate the judgment behind a coherent organizational model.
services.summary: A planned qualification for practitioners applying systemics, GSM modeling and governance through assessed cases and reviewable evidence.
services.lead: A shared modeling language is only useful when practitioners apply it consistently. Organizations and partners need a way to assess whether someone can translate a real situation into coherent definitions, governance and defensible design decisions.
services.proposition: The planned GSM Certification connects conceptual understanding with applied modeling. Practitioners would demonstrate how purposes, functions, interactions and governance fit together, justify their choices and handle ambiguity. Assessment is intended to recognize demonstrated competence rather than course attendance or familiarity with terminology alone.

outcomes.title: Practitioner assurance
outcomes.description: An assessable baseline for systemics, GSM concepts, definition lifecycle and the distinction between definitions and operational reality.

outcomes.title: Partner consistency
outcomes.description: Shared assessment criteria for modeling and governance work, while preserving room for domain-specific knowledge.

outcomes.title: Evidence-led progression
outcomes.description: A proposed progression based on reviewed cases and continuing competence, with credential scope and renewal rules defined before launch.

stages.title: Learn the foundations
stages.description: Develop fluency in systemics, GSM primitives, typing and governance, using a declared version of the model.

stages.title: Demonstrate practice
stages.description: Model realistic cases and explain the assumptions, tradeoffs and governance decisions to an assessor.

stages.title: Maintain standing
stages.description: Follow the planned renewal requirements as the model and assessment framework evolve.
